title: Plan build list is empty for RWB-S8-E2012-APP although the DP table adds eight platform contract rows
source: Work Package B2-S8-017 story line for RWB-S8-E2012-APP (H [], C [RWB-P3-E2012-CON], patterns DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP14, DP15, DP19); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json slice RWB-S8-E2012-APP; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP table
section: Metadata row Depends on (build); section 3 Preconditions; section 13 Pattern application
description: Every pattern of the story adds a platform contract row (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and two C rows (RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON), but the split plan carries no H row at all and one C row only. The story therefore starts on Day 1 against the platform baselines and fakes.
evidence: split_plan.json slice RWB-S8-E2012-APP: H [] and C [RWB-P3-E2012-CON]; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19
proposed: Keep Depends on (build) = None and Ready to start = Day 1 from the plan, carry the eight platform H rows in section 13 as tracked, and let the platform contract stories gate the build at pickup.

title: The operation names and shapes of the consumed contracts other than RWB-P3-E2012-CON are not published
source: RWB-E2-012 section 12 (POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer, GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}, the RuleEvaluator and DecisionLogWriter interfaces); context pack S8 ownership rows; Architecture v5 slide 13
description: The legacy story names one transfer endpoint and one case read; after the split the deviation side also needs the reference-data read of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, the rwb-decision package read, the rwb-access authorise call and the rwb-source-data case-facts read. No source publishes those operation names, paths or schemas for the consumers this story calls.
evidence: RWB-E2-012 section 12 Published interfaces used; context pack S8 ownership rows list two operations provided and no consumed contract; Arch v5 slide 13 gives call types only
proposed: Take each operation from the CON story of its owner as it is published, call them through the generated client, and keep the 2 s budget and the breaker of DP-11.

title: The open-deviation read the P3 slice names is not a row of the Ownership Map, and the S8 event subscription already carries the same fact
source: Work Package B2-S8-017 story line; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2012 APP Manual transfer and reassignment screen with reason v1.md sections 12.2 and 13 (GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations); context pack S8 ownership rows (PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations); Arch v5 slide 13 (P3 listens to S8 events); RWB-E2-012 section 11 (DF-CAS-019 deviation_open read)
section: Section 1 Story; section 12.1 REST operations provided; section 18 Traceability
description: The primary slice in rwb-case states that the move reads the open deviations from rwb-deviation once over REST with a 2 s budget, while the Ownership Map gives S8 two write operations only and the connection matrix has rwb-case listening to S8 events. Two mechanisms describe one fact: a synchronous read of this service and an event-fed flag on recovery_case.
evidence: RWB-P3-E2012-APP section 12.2 row GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations; context pack S8 REST operations provided (2); Arch v5 slide 13 P3 row column S8 = T E; RWB-E2-012 section 11 DF-CAS-019
proposed: Publish GET /cases/{caseId}/deviations on /api/recovery/deviation/v1 as the answer the move and the SCR-05 panel use, keep DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared for the event-fed flag, and fix the read schema in the CON story of this service.

title: The handler rows R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 and the SCR-05 deviation fragment layout are not in the sources
source: FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 (R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-03 only); TSD S8 T4 (rule IDs with no text); RWB-E2-012 section 15 (SCR-05 states, no layout); context pack S8 (no screen row)
section: Section 8 Business rules; section 15 Screens and states
description: The deviation machine names R-DEV-04, R-DEV-05, R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21 as owner-assignment rows for X4 to X7, but no source gives their condition, action or target owner. The SCR-05 deviation fragment has no layout, field order or state drawing in any source.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 table rows R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-03; TSD S8 T4 rows R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 and R-DEV-21; RWB-E2-012 section 15
proposed: Read the four rows from the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook at build time, render the fragment as a table of code, handler, paused state, contact stop and rule ID, and confirm the layout with the screen owner.

title: The event names of the case status and legal-hold changes this service consumes are not published
source: Arch v5 slide 13 (S8 row, column P3 = E); RWB-E2-012 section 4 step 4 (case open and not under a legal hold); context pack S8
description: The connection matrix gives S8 an event subscription to rwb-case and names no event. CaseTransferred is named in the legacy story (EV-04), but the status and legal-hold changes the panel reads have no event name, schema or topic row in any source.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 13 S8 row column P3 = T E; RWB-E2-012 section 4 step 4 and section 14 MSG-P3-005; no event catalogue row for a case status or hold change
proposed: Declare the consumer group against the placeholder, fake it with the platform inbox stub, and bind the published names when the rwb-case event catalogue fixes them.

title: deviation has no transfer reason, rule ID or rule-version column, and the legacy write set is on the rwb-case tables
source: RWB-E2-012 section 11 (DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040, DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-011 written; DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 written through P7); TSD S8 T3.1 (deviation columns DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045); Ownership Map table rows (deviation only)
description: The legacy story writes the queue, team and owner on recovery_case, queue_id and transfer_reason_code on assignment, and the decision log entry through P7, and it reads DF-CAS-019 and DF-CAS-020. The split leaves this service one table, deviation, which holds none of those fields, so the rule ID, the package version and the reason code of a move can only live in the decision record.
evidence: TSD S8 T3.1 columns; RWB-E2-012 section 11 rows DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040, DF-CAS-009 to DF-CAS-011, DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018; context pack S8 table list (deviation)
proposed: Add no column: keep the reason code, the rule ID and the package version in the local decision record, read the case, queue and assignment facts on the rwb-case contract, and confirm with the data owner that the deviation row needs nothing more.

title: The transfer reason codes R01 to R06 are an assumed set pending DL23
source: RWB-E2-012 section 3 (Assumed values: R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral, R06 Wrong queue, DL23); RWB-P3-E2012-APP section 3 (same caveat)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 11 Data; section 14 Validation and messages
description: The reason list LOV-TRANSFER-REASON is named as an assumption in the legacy story and its six values are marked DL23, so the codes and their labels used here are the intended set and not an approved list.
evidence: RWB-E2-012 section 3 bullet LOV-TRANSFER-REASON; RWB-E2-012 section 13 Configuration and reference data; RWB-P3-E2012-APP section 3
proposed: Read the list at its version on the rwb-case reference-data contract, render whatever is in force, and hold the six codes as the default set until DL23 closes.

title: The fifteen legacy test case IDs of RWB-E2-012 are carried by both slices
source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json slices RWB-P3-E2012-APP and RWB-S8-E2012-APP (tcs_legacy TC-E2-012-01 to TC-E2-012-15); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E2012 APP Manual transfer and reassignment screen with reason v1.md section 16; the same ids in this story section 16
description: The split plan gives the same fifteen legacy test case IDs to the rwb-case slice and to this slice. The P3 file carries them at End to end and NFR; this file carries them at Component and NFR as the deviation-side proof, so one ID appears in two story files with two levels.
evidence: split_plan.json tcs_legacy arrays of both slices; RWB-P3-E2012-APP section 16 rows TC-E2-012-01 to TC-E2-012-15
proposed: Keep one row per legacy TC ID in the assembled Test Cases master, record both slices against it, and take the End to end level from the P3 slice and the Component level from this one.
